question: Does a fresh review of the publisher-hosted 2020 Candaba fish-inventory paper change its evidence, traceability, or reuse readiness?

source.citation: Mallari, A. R., Bagunu, J. V., & Salas, G. M. (2020). Fish inventory and fishing practices in Candaba swamp, Philippines: their implication to fishermen's income. Scientific Journal of Tan Trao University, 6(15), 10–16. https://doi.org/10.51453/2354-1431/2020/350
source.accessNote: The official publisher PDF and article metadata page were reviewed. The page currently shows downloads as unavailable even though the publisher PDF URL is fetchable. No local file or checksum is claimed.

studyScope.scopeLimit: The authors identify these two barangays within Candaba Swamp; the paper does not establish the extent of the full swamp or a verified waterbody polygon.
studyScope.samplingAndIdentification: The study describes a descriptive survey of local fisher catches, with morphology-based identification checked by fish experts from the University of the Philippines Los Baños. It says one sample per species group was preserved using taxidermy procedures and deposited at the Biology Museum of the College of Arts and Sciences, Pampanga State Agricultural University.
studyScope.specimenTraceLimit: No museum accession or catalog numbers, digital collection records, specimen-to-source-label crosswalk, or item-level specimen images were found. The reported museum deposit is a lead for future verification, not proof that identified vouchers have been independently inspected.
studyScope.fieldDateLimit: The PDF gives manuscript received and accepted dates, but no field sampling calendar or taxon-by-date record. Editorial dates are not collection dates.
studyScope.countAndTaxonomyLimit: The abstract says 14 species/14 families. A body passage says five Cyprinidae plus ten species from other families, which totals 15; the existing review preserves the source's 14 author-printed name strings. Concatenated and malformed labels remain unnormalized.

erratumAndRights.erratum: The PDF includes an erratum saying the published author list and acknowledgement were incomplete; Gerald M. Salas and the acknowledgements are included in the corrected citation recorded here.
erratumAndRights.publisherPolicyFinding: The current publisher publication-policy page describes a copyright/licensing agreement at submission and says authors retain copyright with some rights. The article page does not show an item-specific Creative Commons license, and its download widget currently reports no downloads available. These pages do not establish a reusable license for this 2020 item.
erratumAndRights.decision: Keep the article and its fish table out of redistributed/app datasets until the applicable item-specific terms are verified. Do not infer the 2020 article's license from other articles or current site-wide examples.

crossSourceReconciliation.decision: Keep the 2020 article's historical two-barangay inventory separate from the 2010 aggregate, 1988 thesis richness, and 2003 thesis lead. The source does not document a whole-swamp, year-round, or current checklist.
crossSourceReconciliation.communityCatchLimit: Local-fisher catches and fishing-practice results are not independent, effort-standardized occurrence or abundance data. They do not establish catchability, current fishing access, safety, legal rules, or diet.

nextAction: If this paper is considered for publication use, first verify article-specific reuse terms and whether PSAU can identify cataloged representatives. In parallel, continue Central Luzon searches for independently reusable Candaba, reservoir, river, estuary, and coastal evidence.

sources.supports: Official article metadata, authors, DOI, abstract, two named barangays, and current download status.
Primary paper methods, study scope, reported museum deposit, count conflict, table, and erratum.
Publisher's general copyright and licensing process; it does not identify an item-specific license for this article.
A separate article page demonstrates the journal's current CC BY-SA item statement; it is not evidence of the 2020 paper's license.
